correctness.rationale: For each local chain factor, two nonzero ideals have nonzero intersection, so product-ideal adjacency is exactly nonempty active-support intersection. The support incidence Gram matrix has the required off-diagonal pattern and rank r because singleton-support ideals supply the standard basis. For r>=2 and one nonfield factor first, the explicit white ideals W1=m1×R2×...×Rr and Wj=0×...×0×Rj×...×Rr are forced successively by singleton-support ideals and finally by W_{r-1}. Thus Z<=N-r, while the Gram witness gives M>=N-r and the standard inequality M<=Z gives equality. The local clique case and K1 boundary are checked separately.

value.rationale: The theorem recovers the number of local factors of a nonreduced finite principal ideal ring from a standard graph inverse-eigenvalue invariant. It simultaneously identifies zero forcing with maximum nullity throughout the regime and provides explicit extremal constructions. This is a structural extension from graph-theoretic ring decompositions to an exact linear-algebraic invariant, not a recomputation of a classical parameter.
